# Issue #112: pointers to keys containing "~" or "/" do not resolve

Given `doc = {"~1": "tilde-one", "a/b": "slash"}`, `resolve(doc, "/~01")` raises `KeyError`,
although `"~01"` is the RFC 6901 encoding of the key `"~1"`. Keys that contain a slash
(`"/a~1b"`) are also affected in some combinations. Plain keys and list indexes work fine.

# Decode each escape once.  Chaining ``replace`` calls would decode the
    # result of the first replacement again, turning ``~01`` into ``/``
    # instead of the required ``~1``.
    decoded = []
    index = 0
    while index < len(token):
        if token[index] == "~" and index + 1 < len(token):
            escape = token[index + 1]
            if escape == "0":
                decoded.append("~")
                index += 2
                continue
            if escape == "1":
                decoded.append("/")
                index += 2
                continue
        decoded.append(token[index])
        index += 1
    return "".join(decoded)
